01Profile

Dr Andrew Hall is a postdoctoral Specialty Registrar in Trauma & Orthopaedic Surgery and Clinical Lecturer at the University of St Andrews (Scottish Clinical Research Excellence Development Scheme). He finished top of the national T&O recruitment and was appointed to the competitive South East Scotland Orthopaedics rotation. He has built experience at high-volume academic institutions, including the major trauma centre at Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh and the national elective orthopaedic centre at the Golden Jubilee University National Hospital. His final two years will focus on knee and hip reconstruction and orthopaedic sports surgery. Uniquely, he is pursuing dual-training to qualify as a Consultant in Sport & Exercise Medicine (SEM).

Dr Hall holds several academic leadership positions, including: Chair of the Scottish Centres for Orthopaedic Treatment & Innovation in Surgery & Healthcare (SCOTTISH) Research Network; Chair of the Scottish Collaborative Orthopaedic Trainees Research Network (SCOTnet), and supervisor for six active PhD and MD students. He is a lead investigator on the MARVEL Project – an ambitious suite of research into robot-assisted orthopaedic surgery (including the field’s largest RCT to date). He has delivered several large national/international studies that have informed practice and government policy, and has published >55 full scientific articles. He holds editorial appointments as Associate Editor (Sports Injury) at the Journal of Science and Medicine in Sport and Guest Editor (Musculoskeletal Sports Injury) at the Journal of Clinical Medicine, and sits on the scientific committee of the Fragility Fracture Network Global Congress 2026. He is a 2024-25 Research Fellow at the British Association of Sport & Exercise Medicine (BASEM) and delivered a nationwide multicentre study evaluating the multisystem health and quality of life impact associated with hip and knee osteoarthritis.

Dr Hall works in multiple high-performance sports medicine environments, including: Team Physician (Heart of Midlothian FC); Match Day Doctor (Scottish Rugby International and Elite Club Teams); Sports Medicine Doctor & Research Fellow (European Tour Performance Institute and DP World Tour Golf), and Committee Member of the Faculty of Sport & Exercise Medicine (Team Care). He is a 2024-25 BASEM Travelling Fellow and, with support from the UK IOC Medical Research Centre, undertook clinical placements at Aspetar (Doha), Mediclinic Perform (Dubai), Sport Surgery Clinic (Dublin), and elite sport environments including European/DP World Tour (Various, International). He holds a PgCert in MSK Ultrasound (with Distinction).

Dr Hall is a committed medical educator and Member of the Faculty of Surgical Trainers (RCSEd). He completed a one-year full-time Medical Education Fellowship and was module organiser for the University of Edinburgh MBChB Musculoskeletal programme. He led a major curriculum overhaul, worked on national working groups, was awarded a PgCert (with Merit) in Clinical Education, and received local/national awards and nominations. He has authored a textbook (published, Scion Publishing) and a textbook chapter (in press, Elsevier), and is associate editor for a third textbook (in press, Elsevier). He was Chief Registrar at the national orthopaedic hospital, has co-hosted several national conferences in orthopaedics, sports medicine, and medical education, and has taught doctors at the Ministry of Health in China. He has an undergraduate degree in psychology (first class honours).

Dr Hall’s final two years of training in T&O surgery (ST7-8) will focus on achieving the FRCS (Tr & Orth), whilst tailoring his subspecialty interests towards knee and hip preservation and reconstruction before undertaking a post-training fellowship in clinical and academic practice in this field. His future practice will be as a clinical and academic T&O surgeon strongly influenced by consultant-level training and experience in high-performance sports medicine.

02Sport & Exercise Medicine

Sport & Exercise Medicine

Dr Hall is pursuing formal dual-accreditation in Trauma & Orthopaedic Surgery (T&O) and Sport & Exercise Medicine (SEM), and is preparing his CESR portfolio for submission for entry to the SEM Specialist Register. His SEM career is built around elite-level clinical experience, research, and international fellowship training, each of which complements and enhances his orthopaedic practice.

He holds a range of clinical roles in high-performance SEM. He is in his sixth season as Team Physician at Heart of Midlothian FC (Men’s & Women’s First Teams and Academy). He is a regular matchday doctor for Scottish Rugby senior international and elite club games, and sports doctor at DP World Tour and Ladies European Tour golf. In 2024–25 he was awarded a BASEM Travelling Fellowship, supported by the UK IOC Medical Research Centre, and completed the STRIKERS Travelling Fellowship in Orthopaedics & Sports Medicine (Surgical Treatment & Rehabilitation of Injuries in Kicking, Explosive & Running Sports). He visited world-class institutions including Aspetar, UPMC Sport Surgery Clinic, Mediclinic Perform, and elite sports physicians in golf, Formula 1, and Olympic sport.

Academically, Dr Hall is a Member of the Faculty of Sport & Exercise Medicine (UK) and has completed both parts of the MFSEM Specialty Exam, in addition to Diplomas in MSK Medicine, Exercise Medicine, and Team Care. He is an examiner for the Diplomas in Team Care and MSK Medicine, a member of the Team Care Committees, and has been part of the FSEM Elite Sport Ethics & Whistleblowing Working Group. He also serves as Professional Development Advisor for the FIFA & University of Bath MSc in Football Medicine and Performance Advisor to the University of St Andrews Performance Sport Programme.

Dr Hall is leading an academic research group at the interface of orthopaedics and sports medicine – investigating themes such as preparing for sustained performance in military environments, evolving trends in physical activity, and the changing landscape of sports-related injuries. He was awarded the 2024-25 BASEM Research Bursary to conduct a multicentre study investigating the multisystem effects of hip and knee osteoarthritis, and his work as Research Fellow at the European Tour Performance Institute focuses on complex issues in high-performance medicine and competitive fairness in elite golf.

03Research

Research

Dr Hall is a postdoctoral Clinical Lecturer on the highly competitive Scottish Clinical Research Excellence Development Scheme (SCREDS). He completed his PhD in 2024 on health data science and outcome prediction in orthopaedics during the COVID-19 pandemic. He supervises six active PhD/MD students, has published >50 peer-reviewed publications and led numerous multicentre and multinational studies that have shaped policy and practice. His research integrates trials, registry, data science, and review methods - a multimodal approach that supports innovation across musculoskeletal healthcare and high-performance sport.

Dr Hall holds national and international academic leadership roles, including Chair of the SCOTTISH Research Network and founder of IMPACT, a global research collaborative established during the COVID-19 pandemic that yielded 16 publications with over 500 co-authors from 20 countries. He has contributed to global benchmarking initiatives and has a strong record of designing and delivering large-scale multicentre studies.

Dr Hall has an established programme of research in knee and hip arthroplasty and sport-related knee injuries. He is Deputy Chief Investigator of the MARVEL Project, the UK’s largest clinical research programme into robot-assisted total knee arthroplasty (VELYS Robot Assisted Solution), and supervises six doctoral candidates whose work includes evaluating and optimising partial and total knee replacement, robotic-assisted surgery, enhanced recovery, sport-related knee injuries, periprosthetic fractures and infection. His research is supported by around £2.5 million in competitive funding, including grants and salaries from UKRI, Johnson & Johnson, BASEM, AO UK&I, Public Health Scotland, and Golden Jubilee University National Hospital. His clinical and translational research extends to interdisciplinary Sports Medicine Event Care and to Performance Medicine, the integrated systems for health and human optimisation that operate in high performance environments, and he leads several multidisciplinary and multifocal projects across both. A related strand examines artificial intelligence and technology enabled interventions for health optimisation, physical activity prescription and injury rehabilitation, together with the development, validation and implementation standards such systems should meet before adoption into healthcare.

As BASEM Research Scholar, Dr Hall’s nationwide SPORT-EMPOWER and WAIT DATA projects evaluate the multisystem health and economic impact of osteoarthritis, and as Research Fellow at the European Tour Performance Institute (ETPI) he works with an elite multidisciplinary sport science team to investigate performance at the highest level. He applies these principles to a growing programme of research into the field of sports medicine and human performance, and continually seeks to push new boundaries at the intersection of medical and scientific fields.

At a specialist tertiary university hospital for children and young people Dr Hall has led data-informed service improvement, educational and governance projects covering emergency department flow and referral management, the multidisciplinary musculoskeletal infection review meeting, the morbidity and mortality meeting, and the multidisciplinary, multiagency major trauma review meeting.

08Education

Medical Education

Dr Hall is a committed medical educator and Member of the Faculty of Surgical Trainers (RCSEd). He completed a year-long full-time Medical Education Fellowship, leading major curriculum overhaul of the University of Edinburgh’s MBChB Musculoskeletal programme and earning a PgCert in Clinical Education (with Merit). His work received national recognition, including a Highly Commended Innovation in Training Award and an Outstanding Role Model nomination from NHS Education for Scotland.

He has authored a published textbook (The Surgical Portfolio and Interview), contributed to The Unofficial Guide to Paediatrics (Elsevier, in press), and is Associate Editor of The Unofficial Guide to Orthopaedics (Elsevier, in press). He has published eight articles on medical education covering surgical training, virtual learning, SEM education, and equality and culture. As Chief Registrar at the national orthopaedic hospital, he led postgraduate teaching strategy and now supervises six active PhD/MD candidates. His academic background in psychology (First Class Honours) supports a learner-centred, evidence-based approach across the educational spectrum. He has held regional and national roles coordinating postgraduate training in surgery and medicine.

Dr Hall co-designed the Performance Curriculum for the University of St Andrews Performance Sport Programme – a suite of educational materials for athletes, coaches, and support staff aimed at optimising athletic health and performance. As a Professional Development Advisor he has taught sports medicine practice to FIFA & University of Bath masters students. He examines on the Faculty of Sport & Exercise Medicine’s Diploma in MSK Medicine, and sits on the sub-group overseeing the Diploma in Team Care. He has held roles across undergraduate and postgraduate education, including tutor, course organiser, and examiner. He has co-organised national conferences in SEM, orthopaedics, and professional culture, and designed national simulation and skills programmes for NHS Lothian and NHS Education for Scotland. He has also taught at the Ministry of Health in China. He is currently designing a multidisciplinary, multispecialty postgraduate training placement spanning Spinal Surgery, Interventional Radiology and Rehabilitation Services, and an interdisciplinary professional education programme in Sports Medicine Event Care and Performance Medicine delivering clinical and research skills online and in person.
